title: Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study with 100+ NLP Researchers
input: One of seven prompting-focused NLP topics; the AI agent additionally retrieves/ranks relevant paper titles and abstracts, while humans and models receive the same topic description, template, and demonstration.
output_unit: Full project proposal: title, problem statement, motivation, proposed method, step-by-step experiment plan, test-case examples, and fallback plan.
answer_key: No future-paper gold for main ideation comparison; human expert review scores are the reference signal.
evaluation: Blind expert review of individual anonymized/style-normalized proposals. Each dimension and overall quality receive a 1–10 score plus rationale. Separate agent-internal pairwise Swiss tournament ranks generated ideas.
reliability: order_reversal=no; position_bias=no; calibration=Clear 1–10 anchors; human split-half consistency; LLM–human agreement benchmark (best pairwise LLM 53.3%).
human_grounding: sample=49 ideas per condition; 298 unique reviews; 2–4 reviewers per idea; reviewer-level comparison reports N=70 for AI-vs-human novelty; 100+ researchers overall.; agreement=yes: split-half top/bottom-quartile consistency 56.1% (20 random splits); compared with ICLR 71.9%.
leakage: Novelty rubric asks reviewers to treat work online before July 2024 as prior art; ideas are style-normalized and blinded.
scope: Expert-perceived novelty, excitement, feasibility, expected effectiveness, and overall proposal quality; head-to-head human-vs-LLM ideation study.
falsifiability: required=generic_testability_only; notes=Fallback-plan language is post-failure contingency, not an explicit falsifying result or decision rule. No exact A/B reverse-order audit was found for the internal Swiss ranker.
closest_overlap_with_lit2test: Literature-grounded research proposals with executable experiment plans, named datasets/models/metrics, expert feasibility ratings, and no future-paper answer key.
key_difference_from_lit2test: The proposal asks for a fallback plan and positive test examples, but not a precommitted observable result that would reject the hypothesis; main measurement is scalar human review, not order-audited pairwise judgment of a minimal falsifiable test.

title: AI Idea Bench 2025: AI Research Idea Generation Benchmark
input: A target paper’s anonymized topic plus contents of papers that inspired/motivated it.
output_unit: Research-idea motivation and multi-step experimental plan.
answer_key: Target-paper motivation and experiment plan are the correct MCQ answer and similarity reference.
evaluation: Six evaluations: target-paper MCQ; idea-to-idea and idea-to-topic 1–5 matching; DeepSeek-V3 pairwise competition on six aspects; literature-distance novelty; citation-derived feasibility and per-step feasibility.
reliability: order_reversal=no; position_bias=Prompt says “Avoid any position biases,” but no swap/reverse experiment or statistic is reported.; calibration=none reported
leakage: Target papers after 2023-10-03, aligned with GPT-4o cutoff; preprint dates filtered.
scope: Recovery/alignment to the hidden target paper, relative idea quality, novelty against historical/contemporary literature, and feasibility via related-method citation influence.
falsifiability: required=no; notes=No falsifier-family keyword appeared in the main/appendix prompts. Feasibility is a citation-influence proxy rather than whether a decisive experiment can reject the hypothesis.
closest_overlap_with_lit2test: Inspired-paper context, full motivation+experiment-plan output, pairwise judging, explicit attention to leakage.
key_difference_from_lit2test: Uses target-paper content as ground truth and later-paper/reference signals; experiment plan has no required decisive metric or bidirectional supporting/falsifying outcomes; pairwise order is only instructed, not audited.

title: HARPA: A Testability-Driven, Literature-Grounded Framework for Research Ideation
input: A user-selected source paper; a citation-linked reasoning chain and literature snippets; an initial/seed hypothesis; target ASD-agent capability constraints.
output_unit: A full hypothesis-driven research proposal: research gap/question, concrete hypothesis, long description, variables, design/implementation, metrics, baselines, pilot, and resources.
answer_key: CodeScientist execution logs/outcome categories for feasibility scorer; no unique future-paper answer key for generated proposal quality.
evaluation: Human experts give 10-point Likert ratings on 11 dimensions; CodeScientist executes proposals; execution traces are labeled success/failure/uncertain; a learned pairwise scorer predicts execution feasibility.
reliability: order_reversal=no; position_bias=no; calibration=Scorer is trained against execution-derived success/failure preferences; held-out accuracy and rubric-wise oracle consistency are reported.
human_grounding: sample=12 experts; 40 proposals per system overall, each source-paper expert rates the four proposals for that source; agreement=No cross-rater agreement: proposals were topic/expert-specific and not cross-reviewed.
leakage: Human source papers had >=20 citations and were published before 2025; no reported contamination audit for proposal content.
scope: Literature-grounded, testable, feasible hypothesis/proposal generation for downstream automated scientific discovery agents.
falsifiability: required=generic_testability_only; notes=Focused scan found no falsif/disconfirm/refut/failure-condition/decision-rule/supporting-result phrase in full paper. `reject` concerns post-execution meta-analysis or filtering, not a required pre-execution falsifier. Under the plan strict rule, required metrics, controls, expected outcomes, and success interpretation count only as generic testability; post-hoc support/reject states do not qualify as `partial`. Human evaluation randomizes proposal display order but does not run A/B reversal. Verify any post-v1 artifact/revision before final submission.
closest_overlap_with_lit2test: Literature-grounded gap/hypothesis, required experiment design and metrics, controls/baselines, pilot-scale execution, and support/reject outcome representation.
key_difference_from_lit2test: HARPA requires metrics and expected-success interpretation but does not precommit a separate observable falsifying-result field. Rejection is assigned post hoc from executed results; its primary target is executable proposal generation and success prediction, not prospective judging of a bidirectional decision rule.

title: IdeaBench: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Research Idea Generation
input: Abstracts of references cited by a 2024 biomedical target paper; low-resource mode uses five filtered references and high-resource mode uses all references.
output_unit: One brief, concise hypothesis/research-idea paragraph per query (three generated ideas in experiments).
answer_key: The target paper’s abstract is summarized into the reference idea; its cited references are the generation context.
evaluation: GPT-4o listwise ranks three generated ideas together with an LLM-extracted target-paper idea under a user-defined quality indicator; target rank is converted to Insight Score. BERTScore and GPT-4o idea-overlap score provide similarity diagnostics.
reliability: order_reversal=no; position_bias=no; the published prompt places the target-paper idea first (Hypothesis 1).; calibration=none
human_grounding: sample=No systematic human calibration; humans highlight qualitative examples only.; agreement=no
leakage: Target papers published in 2024; tested model cutoffs reported before 2024.
scope: Generation aligned with the target-paper trajectory plus novelty/feasibility relative to the hidden target-paper idea.
falsifiability: required=no; notes=Negative claims are E3 from main+appendix keyword/prompt scan. Artifact was unavailable, so implementation-level randomization cannot be ruled out beyond the published prompt.
closest_overlap_with_lit2test: Real-paper local neighborhood and generation before seeing the target paper.
key_difference_from_lit2test: Uses one target paper as a relative answer key and produces a generic hypothesis paragraph; no minimal test, decisive metric, supporting/falsifying result, human calibration, or order control.

title: Predicting Empirical AI Research Outcomes with Language Models
input: Research goal defined by benchmarks/quantitative metrics plus two standardized detailed idea descriptions; optional cutoff-limited retrieved papers.
output_unit: Binary prediction of which idea performs better; optional rationale.
decision_rule: minimal_test=no; decisive_metric=yes (provided benchmark outcomes); support=no; falsifier=no; controls=no
evaluation: 6,000 historical training pairs and 1,585 human-verified post-cutoff test pairs; two predictions with swapped idea order, inconsistency counted wrong; separate expert baseline on 45 NLP pairs.
reliability: order_reversal=yes; position_bias=yes: inconsistent swaps invalid/incorrect.; calibration=Human expert baseline, robustness stress tests, exact empirical gold.
human_grounding: sample=16 student verifiers for 1,585 examples; 25 topic experts on 45 pairs, 222 valid annotations.; agreement=yes: expert-to-majority agreement 75.1%.
leakage: GPT-4.1 cutoff June 1 2024; every test example has at least one later idea; retrieval restricted before cutoff.
scope: Forecasting empirical AI research outcomes before execution.
falsifiability: required=no; notes=Objective winner is an external label derived after execution, not the proposal’s own precommitted decision rule.
closest_overlap_with_lit2test: Pairwise idea judgment, exact A/B reversal, human calibration, and objective experiment-related signals.
key_difference_from_lit2test: Predicts which already-realized method wins on supplied benchmarks; no generator-produced minimal test or supporting/falsifying decision rule.

title: Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist
input: A scientist-defined natural-language research goal, optional long documents/private evidence, desired attributes/constraints, and ongoing scientist feedback.
output_unit: Iteratively generated and ranked hypotheses/research proposals, sometimes experimental protocols; final top hypotheses/reviews are synthesized into a research overview.
answer_key: No single future-paper answer key; some component checks use GPQA/paper-QA correctness, while biomedical case studies use expert judgment and experimental outcomes.
evaluation: Internal Reflection reviews and Elo pairwise tournaments; automated evaluation over 203 goals and 15 expert-curated goals; blinded small expert comparison on 11 goals; selected real hypotheses undergo expert curation and wet-lab validation; clinical Specific Aims study uses 78 proposals and nine oncologists.
reliability: order_reversal=yes; position_bias=yes: Supplementary Note 3 tests 2,000 matches with A/B and B/A presentations; Supplementary Figs. 4-5 report improved positional robustness from scientific debate prompting; calibration=GPQA/paper-QA ablations relate Elo/review scores to correctness; A/B reversal probes position bias; external LLM panel and blinded experts provide orthogonal checks.
human_grounding: sample=Main comparison: curator experts on 11 research goals, typically the goal's expert; clinical evaluation: nine hematologist/oncologists in two groups rating 78 unique hypotheses; wet-lab selections were expert-screened.; agreement=No inter-rater agreement for the 11-goal main comparison. Clinical two-group ratings report Spearman rho=0.745 (p<0.001), not item-level annotator reliability.
leakage: Reflection uses web search and can use private/unpublished evidence; novelty ablations test search/date cutoffs. No benchmark-wide fixed temporal split for open hypothesis tasks.
scope: Scientist-in-the-loop generation of novel, plausible, testable, safe scientific hypotheses and research plans; this is a research system, not a fixed public benchmark task.
falsifiability: required=partial; notes=Strict classification: `partial`, not `yes`. The disproof field is required and judgeable, so `generic_testability_only` would understate overlap. It evaluates whether existing observations contradict the hypothesis; it does not require the hypothesis author to precommit what a future decisive experiment would observe if the proposal were false. Weakness/limitation prompts and observed experimental failure discussion are not counted as falsifiers. The broad wording `first to operationalize falsifiability` is unsafe after this check.
closest_overlap_with_lit2test: Explicit testability criterion; generation prompt requests anticipated outcomes; mandatory Reflection prompt performs structured disproof analysis and can label a hypothesis `disproved`; pairwise ranking is tested under A/B reversal.
key_difference_from_lit2test: Co-Scientist's submitted/generated proposal does not have to precommit a future observable falsifying condition or a bidirectional decision rule. Its required `disproof analysis` is an internal reviewer step over already available article observations; experimental protocols and metrics depend on the scientist's goal. The work is a generative research system with heterogeneous downstream validations, not a benchmark whose answer schema judges a falsifier field.

title: Evaluating LLMs' Divergent Thinking Capabilities for Scientific Idea Generation with Minimal Context
input: A single scientific keyword drawn from 1,180 keywords across 22 domains; no paper neighborhood.
output_unit: A scientific idea in at most 100 target words (200-word hard exclusion threshold).
answer_key: Rubric-based judge panel; same rubric human subset.
evaluation: Each idea independently scored 1–10 by three randomly sampled eligible LLM judges on originality/feasibility/clarity; a separate pair-comparison judge grades within-keyword idea similarity for fluency; flexibility is the 30th percentile of composite performance. Generator is excluded from its own panel.
reliability: order_reversal=no; position_bias=no; human questionnaire order randomized, but no exact pair reversal.; calibration=PDE expert validation; human–LLM Pearson correlations; ICC; generator excluded from own evaluation.
human_grounding: sample=22 PDE ideas × 6 domain experts.; agreement=yes: ICC(A,k) originality 0.823, clarity 0.782, feasibility 0.453.
leakage: Monthly keyword/model refresh; self-evaluation excluded; not a paper-answer-key design.
scope: Divergent-thinking scientific ideation: originality, feasibility, clarity, fluency, and flexibility.
falsifiability: required=no; notes=The introduction calls scientific ideas testable, but neither generator prompt nor critic schema requests a test or a falsifying outcome.
closest_overlap_with_lit2test: No future-paper answer key, explicit multidimensional judge protocol, ensemble judging, and a bounded human calibration subset.
key_difference_from_lit2test: Keyword-only divergent ideation, not literature-neighborhood-conditioned minimal tests; no required experiment, decisive metric, or supporting/falsifying outcome; no forward/reverse pairwise audit.

title: HindSight: Evaluating LLM-Generated Research Ideas via Future Impact
input: Pre-cutoff literature/topic or seed paper; generator restricted to pre-T papers.
output_unit: Generated problem statement plus proposed method; evaluator matches it to post-T publications.
decision_rule: minimal_test=no; decisive_metric=yes (external evaluator metric); support=no; falsifier=no; controls=no
evaluation: 200 ideas across 10 topics; SPECTER2 matching to 27,589 post-cutoff papers; impact = 0.6 normalized citations + 0.4 top-venue; compared with repeated pointwise LLM ratings.
reliability: order_reversal=no; position_bias=no; calibration=Compares LLM judge to future-impact signal; no human calibration.
leakage: T=June 2023; generation sees only pre-T literature; post-T June 2023–Dec 2025 ground-truth pool.
scope: Whether ideas anticipate later real research directions and impact.
falsifiability: required=no; notes=The plan says HorizonBench, but exact-title HorizonBench is unrelated personalization. HindSight is the scientifically relevant likely alias.
closest_overlap_with_lit2test: Evaluates model-generated ideas temporally and avoids relying only on an LLM judge.
key_difference_from_lit2test: Treats realized future publications as answer keys and may reward trajectory/surface alignment; does not require experiment design or falsifying outcomes.

title: HypoBench: Towards Systematic and Principled Benchmarking for Hypothesis Generation
input: A phenomenon/task, labeled observational data, and optionally relevant literature; 7 real tasks and 5 synthetic tasks across 194 datasets.
output_unit: A bank/list of natural-language hypotheses that explain feature-outcome relationships; task implementations sometimes request paired positive/opposite predictive hypotheses.
answer_key: Ground-truth synthetic hypotheses and held-out outcome labels; no future-paper answer key.
evaluation: Held-out hypothesis-based prediction accuracy/F1; synthetic feature-discovery rate × relationship correctness (HDR); GPT-4o 1–5 ratings of novelty/plausibility/clarity for real datasets; OOD and cross-model tests.
reliability: order_reversal=no; position_bias=no; calibration=Two humans independently annotate 100 hidden-score pairs; agreement with each other and the model is reported.
human_grounding: sample=100 hypothesis pairs, two annotators, stratified across task categories and score ranges; agreement=Yes: FDR human-human Cohen kappa 0.80; RC weighted kappa 0.86. Model-human 0.71 and 0.64, respectively.
leakage: IND/OOD splits by source/domain are reported; synthetic difficulty/counterintuitive variants probe priors; no model-training contamination audit.
scope: Generating interpretable explanations of observed phenomena, explicitly distinguished from literature-driven research ideation.
falsifiability: required=no; notes=Full-text and artifact scan found no falsif/disconfirm/refut/failure-condition/decision-rule/supporting-result requirement. The artifact's positive/opposite hypothesis pairs predict both outcome classes; they are not experiment-contingent observations that would reject a research proposal. `Could this be tested?` is an optional judge consideration under plausibility, hence not a falsifier field. Use 2026 for v2/current citation status but retain original 2025 posting date in BibTeX notes if needed.
closest_overlap_with_lit2test: A 2026 benchmark with natural-language hypotheses, optional literature grounding, testability language in the plausibility rubric, human-calibrated LLM judging, and no future-paper key.
key_difference_from_lit2test: HypoBench defines a hypothesis as an explanation of observed labeled phenomena and scores it by predictive utility/ground-truth recovery. It asks for hypotheses, not a next-step experiment, decisive metric, or precommitted supporting/falsifying outcomes.

title: InnoEval: On Research Idea Evaluation as a Knowledge-Grounded, Multi-Perspective Reasoning Problem
input: Raw idea plus optional timestamp; extraction yields TLDR, motivation, research question, methods, experiment settings, and optional expected results; system retrieves literature/web/code.
output_unit: Pointwise multi-dimensional review and decision, or groupwise ranking; revision suggestions.
answer_key: Conference decision tier, not a future paper.
evaluation: 217 ideas extracted from ICLR/NeurIPS 2025 papers labeled Reject/Poster/Spotlight/Oral; 372 pairwise and 172 groupwise instances. Five randomized reviewer personas each score five dimensions 0–10; report agent predicts decision/ranking.
reliability: order_reversal=no; position_bias=no; calibration=Correlation with expert scores and LLM-extracted peer-review scores; decision labels from conferences.
human_grounding: sample=5 experts (3 PhD students, 1 professor, 1 algorithm engineer) score 60 ideas.; agreement=Pearson correlations to mean human scores reported (all ≥0.5); no inter-human coefficient.
leakage: Idea timestamp separates pre-knowledge for evaluation from post-knowledge for suggestions.
scope: Knowledge-grounded, multi-perspective idea evaluation aligned with conference outcomes and human dimension scores.
falsifiability: required=no; notes=Post-timestamp papers do not define the decision label but do influence revision advice. Expected results are optional and one-directional, not an explicit falsifier.
closest_overlap_with_lit2test: Structured research-plan input, multi-dimensional judging, pair/group comparisons, timestamps, heterogeneous evidence, and human alignment study.
key_difference_from_lit2test: Measures prediction of conference outcomes/ratings from retrospectively extracted papers; expected results are optional and no bidirectional decision rule or explicit falsifying outcome is required; no order-reversal audit.

title: Is this Idea Novel? An Automated Benchmark for Judgment of Research Ideas
input: Structured research idea (problem, objective, solution approach) plus titles/abstracts of cited related works.
output_unit: Novelty score 1–5 plus short literature-grounded textual justification.
answer_key: Human expert novelty scores/arguments and cited related works.
evaluation: 1,381 ICLR 2022/2023 ideas; macro-F1/MAE for scores plus seven justification metrics for alignment, known/novel-aspect recall/addition/hallucination.
reliability: order_reversal=no; position_bias=no; calibration=Direct comparison with human scores and human-derived rationales; grounding quality filter.
human_grounding: sample=6,410 submissions initially; ~3 expert reviews each; 3,535 high-agreement submissions before final 1,381 after processing/filtering.; agreement=Filter-based only: max disagreement ≤1 across both novelty dimensions; no kappa/ICC.
leakage: No prospective split; only cited related works from introduction/related-work sections are supplied.
scope: Alignment of automatic research-idea novelty judgments with expert peer-review judgments and rationales.
falsifiability: required=no; notes=RINoBench is the plan’s RINoBench seed. It is not a generation or experiment-design benchmark.
closest_overlap_with_lit2test: Human-labeled open-ended research-idea judgments with literature context and explicit rationales.
key_difference_from_lit2test: Only judges novelty of a generic idea representation; no experiment, metric, minimal test, supporting result, falsifying result, pairwise reliability, or order controls.

title: On the Limits of LLM-as-Judge for Scientific Novelty Assessment
input: Influential cited background papers (with section text), grounded gaps, and author-anchored research question reconstructed from a recent source paper.
output_unit: Exactly five generated research questions; judges score each question on novelty/scope or compare it listwise.
answer_key: Target/source paper’s pursued research question is a reference point, explicitly not the only valid question.
evaluation: 1,434 author-anchored RQs from 746 papers; standalone and listwise comparative scores on originality/gap-addressing/non-obviousness; two LLM judges and blinded two-expert study on 50 cs.CL/cs.LG cases.
reliability: order_reversal=no; position_bias=no candidate-order randomization/reversal reported.; calibration=Direct blinded human comparison on same non-obviousness rubric; extracted-RQ faithfulness: 50/50 human approved.
human_grounding: sample=2 domain experts × 50 blinded comparisons (repeated with alternate prompt on 50).; agreement=yes: expert–expert 60% original study (54% alternate prompt); LLM–LLM 52%/62%; expert–LLM as low as 22%.
leakage: Recent 2025–2026 arXiv source papers; author-anchor overlap reported as memorization diagnostic.
scope: Research-question generation and reliability of LLM-as-judge for scientific novelty.
falsifiability: required=no; notes=The narrowness rubric calls some outputs “diagnostic/test-list framing,” but that is a scope judgment, not a requirement to state falsifying outcomes.
closest_overlap_with_lit2test: Local real-paper background, no assumption that the author-anchored continuation is unique, multi-judge and human-alignment analysis.
key_difference_from_lit2test: Outputs research questions rather than testable proposals; target-paper RQ remains a reference; no minimal experiment, metric, supporting result, or falsifying outcome; no order reversal.

title: Proof of Time: A Benchmark for Evaluating Scientific Idea Judgments
input: Frozen pre-cutoff evidence snapshots for papers, authors, or benchmark leaderboards in an offline sandbox.
output_unit: MCQ, ranking, or bucket forecast of citations, awards, faculty research direction, or future SOTA.
decision_rule: minimal_test=no; decisive_metric=yes (external task label); support=no; falsifier=no; controls=no
evaluation: Over 30K instances in four domains; exact-match against post-cutoff signals; direct and tool-using agent conditions with budget/tool ablations.
leakage: Formal E≤t0 versus yt1 split; network-disabled read-only sandbox.
scope: Future-facing scientific judgment tied to later observable impact/value/evolution signals.
falsifiability: required=no; notes=PoT is an idea-judgment/forecasting benchmark, not idea generation. It demonstrates that no-future-label design is a trade-off, not a universal norm.
closest_overlap_with_lit2test: Prospective/temporal evaluation and discrete future-verifiable outcomes rather than subjective LLM judge labels.
key_difference_from_lit2test: Forecasts realized downstream signals and does not generate or judge a minimal falsifiable test; later outcomes are explicit answer keys.

title: ResearchBench: Benchmarking LLMs in Scientific Discovery via Inspiration-Based Task Decomposition
input: Target paper decomposed into research question, background survey, ground-truth inspiration papers, and ground-truth hypothesis; negative inspiration papers sampled at three semantic/domain distances.
output_unit: Retrieved inspiration set; composed hypothesis; pairwise judgment between ground-truth and negative hypotheses.
answer_key: The target paper’s hypothesis and inspiration papers.
evaluation: Retrieval accuracy; generated-hypothesis matched score on a 0–5 Likert scale against target key points; ground-truth-vs-negative pairwise ranking repeated in both orders.
reliability: order_reversal=yes: every hypothesis pair compared twice with reverse positions.; position_bias=yes: Table 6 reports both-wrong/one-right/both-right; some models self-contradict up to 91.67%.; calibration=Expert validation of decomposition, necessity, and sufficiency; no calibration of ranking judge to human preference.
human_grounding: sample=5 PhD experts; 62 sampled papers; domain assignment means little overlap.; agreement=no: authors explicitly state experts rarely reviewed the same papers.
leakage: 2024+ target papers; stricter post-July-2024 subset analysis in Appendix A.1.
scope: Inspiration retrieval, hypothesis composition, and hypothesis ranking as a sufficient decomposition of scientific discovery.
falsifiability: required=no; notes=A.5 asks which hypothesis would be more effective if tested, but does not request a test design or falsifying observation.
closest_overlap_with_lit2test: Real-paper decomposition, hypothesis generation, pairwise comparison, explicit reverse-order evaluation, and contamination-aware construction.
key_difference_from_lit2test: Measures recovery/ranking of the target-paper hypothesis, not prospective minimal-test formulation; no experiment plan, decisive metric, supporting result, or falsifying outcome.

title: ResearchStudio-Idea: An Evidence-Grounded Research-Ideation Skill Suite from ML Conference Outcomes
input: Under-specified user research direction plus live, multi-source retrieved literature and an evidence bundle; 15/31 conference-outcome-derived ideation patterns guide the workflow.
output_unit: One proposal artifact bundle/idea card with motivation, method flow, core claim, compute budget, feasibility validation, and mandatory falsification_prediction; possible stop/abandon instead of an idea.
answer_key: No unique future-paper answer key for scoring; closest literature and normalized proposals are judged automatically.
evaluation: 100 title-only method-agnostic ICLR-2026-Oral seeds; four systems; outputs normalized to Title/Motivation/Method; blind listwise quality ranking and prior-art novelty scoring, three fresh rounds with per-seed/per-round random labels.
reliability: order_reversal=randomized_per_round_not_exact_reverse; position_bias=controlled by a fresh random label permutation per seed and round; no separate residual-bias statistic.; calibration=No human calibration; format/length/equation normalization and blind repeated randomization.
leakage: Induction corpus 2021–2025; held-out ICLR-2026 Oral title-only seeds; live collision retrieval; source identity withheld.
scope: A reusable evidence-grounded ideation skill/system; endpoint generation quality and novelty are evaluated, not falsifier-formulation capability itself.
falsifiability: required=yes; notes=Schema nuance: positive result direction is required. The falsifying discriminator is the negative-control intervention returning the downstream outcome toward baseline; it is a mechanism falsifier rather than a separate free-standing “falsifying_result” field. Byte identity is strict Phase2→Phase4 and Phase2→Phase3→Phase4 on revise paths, except an explicitly audited rewrite_falsification operation can re-base the Phase3→Phase4 commitment. Thus prior-system absence is unsafe; only a qualified claim about the complete minimal-falsifiable-test contract as a joint benchmark unit remains plausible.
closest_overlap_with_lit2test: Direct positive match: requires a minimal experiment, named downstream metric and supporting direction, a named load-bearing variable, and a non-tautological negative-control intervention whose downstream outcome distinguishes the mechanism.
key_difference_from_lit2test: It is a retrieval- and audit-augmented research-ideation skill whose falsification prediction acts as a generation-time safeguard. Endpoint evaluation normalizes to Title/Motivation/Method, so judges do not see or score falsification_prediction. Lit2Test instead compares the complete contract holistically under a fixed literature context; this is an evaluation-unit distinction, not an isolated falsifier score.

title: ScholarEval: Research Idea Evaluation Grounded in Literature
input: A research idea with Problem, Methods, and Experiments, plus a cutoff date; system retrieves literature.
output_unit: Long-form citation-grounded soundness and contribution review with strengths, weaknesses, and actionable suggestions.
answer_key: Human peer-review points restricted to aspects knowable at ideation stage.
evaluation: ScholarIdeas contains 117 retrospectively extracted ideas and 1,076 expert-validated review rubrics. Coverage uses Prometheus 1–5 per rubric. Claude-4-Sonnet pairwise-compares ScholarEval vs baselines on evidence, actionability, and depth; human study validates judge and usefulness.
reliability: order_reversal=no; position_bias=no; calibration=Human pairwise replication with same rubric; expert user study; source validity audit.
human_grounding: sample=6 experts validate 117 idea/rubric pairs; judge calibration: 6 PhD students over 33 report pairs (18 non-split); user study: 18 experts and 46 evaluations.; agreement=yes: human–LLM percent agreement/Gwet AC1 = 66.67%/0.4476 evidence, 72.22%/0.1667 actionability, 61.11%/0.3883 depth.
leakage: First submission/review versions; results sections dropped; paper publication date used as retrieval cutoff.
scope: Coverage and quality of pre-execution research-idea evaluation.
falsifiability: required=no; notes=Soundness retrieval extracts supporting/contradicting literature evidence, which is not the same as requiring the proposal to state an outcome that would falsify its own hypothesis.
closest_overlap_with_lit2test: Pre-execution idea review, literature grounding, explicit soundness/experimental-plan critique, cutoff-aware evidence, and bounded human calibration.
key_difference_from_lit2test: Judges already-written full plans and outputs feedback; it does not ask a generator to formulate a minimal test or precommit supporting/falsifying outcomes, and its primary automatic pairwise judge compares review reports rather than ideas.

title: SoundnessBench: Can Your AI Scientist Really Tell Good Research Ideas from Bad Ones?
input: Results-masked, near-verbatim ICLR proposal represented as hypothesis and experiment description; source paper used only for construction/audit.
output_unit: Binary low/high soundness label, 1–5 confidence, and detailed justification.
answer_key: Expert reviewer soundness proxy from completed source papers, with results masked from model input.
evaluation: 1,099 proposals labeled from reviewer soundness sub-scores; 12 LLMs under standard and aggressive prompts; contamination, identifier, surface-feature, slice, and adversarial-content controls.
reliability: order_reversal=no; position_bias=no; calibration=Prompt-framing stress test plus multiple confounder controls and preliminary human audit.
human_grounding: sample=Preliminary audit: 2 annotators, balanced 60-proposal subset.; agreement=Reports 92.3% expected-No leakage checks and 84.6% expected-Yes label defensibility; not a full inter-rater coefficient.
leakage: Results/outcome/acceptance cues removed; ICLR-2026 subset with cutoff-restricted models; identifier-removal tests.
scope: Recoverable proposal-stage methodological soundness: whether a design can rigorously test its hypothesis.
falsifiability: required=generic_testability_only; notes=Classified generic_testability_only: falsification is discussed as a soundness principle, but no explicit result/threshold/intervention field is required or judged.
closest_overlap_with_lit2test: Very close construct boundary: pre-execution hypothesis–experiment rigor, controls, baselines, metrics, and language that a design should validate or falsify a claim.
key_difference_from_lit2test: Neither input schema nor output requires the proposer to name an observable falsifying outcome. The judge predicts peer-review-derived soundness rather than comparing explicit bidirectional decision rules; no pairwise/order audit.

title: Teaching Language Models to Forecast Research Success Through Comparative Idea Evaluation
input: Benchmark-specific research goal and two detailed paper-grounded method descriptions.
output_unit: Binary better-performing idea label, optionally preceded by reasoning trace.
decision_rule: minimal_test=no; decisive_metric=yes (provided benchmark metric); support=no; falsifier=no; controls=no
evaluation: 11,488 pairs/724 leaderboards; unified metric score and sigma difficulty; both original and swapped pairs; accuracy requires consistency across order.
